claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 dose-finding trial in adults with overweight/obesity without diabetes (n=387), 46 weeks of once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide produced placebo-corrected body-weight reductions ranging from -3.4% at the 0.6 mg dose to -12.1% at the 4.8 mg dose (both statistically significant), with the 4.8 mg group reaching -14.9% weight change versus -2.8% for placebo; gastrointestinal adverse events were substantially more common with survodutide, and treatment discontinuation due to adverse events was markedly higher than placebo.

claims.statement: The primary peer-reviewed phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 results (76-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in n=725 adults with obesity without type 2 diabetes; published in the New England Journal of Medicine, PMID 42253238, doi 10.1056/nejmoa2600751) report mean body-weight change from baseline to week 76 of -12.2% with survodutide 3.6 mg and -13.0% with survodutide 6.0 mg, versus -5.4% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand; P<0.001 for both active doses vs placebo); 72.6% (3.6 mg), 71.9% (6.0 mg), and 46.3% (placebo) of participants achieved at least 5% weight loss. These verified primary-source figures supersede an earlier ConscienHealth secondary-summary topline of approximately 16.6% vs approximately 3.2%, which is now understood to have overstated the drug-arm effect and understated the placebo effect relative to the published peer-reviewed result (the discrepancy's exact source -- e.g., a different interim analysis population, a non-estimand-adjusted announcement figure, or reporting error in the secondary summary -- was not further investigated in this pass and is not asserted here).

context.population: adults with obesity or overweight with >=1 weight-related complication, without type 2 diabetes
context.formulation: survodutide 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg once weekly vs placebo
context.doseText: survodutide 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg once weekly with up-titration, 76-week trial protocol (SYNCHRONIZE-1); not a use recommendation

extractedEvidence.quote: At week 76, the mean change in body weight from baseline according to the treatment-regimen estimand was -12.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -13.6 to -10.8) in the 3.6-mg group, -13.0% (95% CI, -14.4 to -11.6) in the 6.0-mg group, and -5.4% (95% CI, -6.9 to -4.0) in the placebo group; 72.6%, 71.9% and 46.3% of the participants, respectively, had weight reduction of at least 5% (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo).

The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal symptoms (typically mild to moderate), which occurred in 80.9% of the participants in the 3.6-mg group, in 89.7% of those in the 6.0-mg group, and in 47.9% of those in the placebo group. No deaths were reported.

claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in adults with MASH and fibrosis, survodutide was superior to placebo for the primary histologic endpoint (improvement in MASH without worsening of fibrosis): 47% (2.4 mg), 62% (4.8 mg), and 43% (6.0 mg) of survodutide-treated patients met the endpoint versus 14% of placebo-treated patients; gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, diarrhea, vomiting) were substantially more frequent with survodutide, and discontinuation due to adverse events occurred in 20% of survodutide-treated patients versus 3% of placebo-treated patients.

context.population: adults with biopsy-confirmed MASH and fibrosis stages F1-F3
context.formulation: survodutide 2.4 mg, 4.8 mg, or 6.0 mg once weekly vs placebo
context.doseText: 2.4-6.0 mg once weekly with rapid dose-escalation phase, 48-week trial protocol; not a use recommendation
